messages:
Incident-Bot: [ALERT] High tail latency detected on /v1/chat/stream (pool=shared-gpu-2). p95=350ms -> 1.1s, p99=900ms -> 3.6s in last 12m. Paging oncall Alex.
Alex: oncall here, looking. any initial triage pointers?
Priya: seeing sustained blkio.write_bytes on gpu-host-07 coincident with kernel writeback spikes. I/O wait jumping to 40% on that host. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/pool-sharedgpus/io-latency?from=now-1h
Diego: traces show streaming sessions stuck waiting on disk flush at runtime; logs show repeated fsyncs from tenant 'alpha-analytics'. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:14:03Z host=gpu-host-07 tenant=alpha-analytics syslog: sync_child: writing checkpoint 6.1GB
```
Maya: p99 tail increase also aligns with KV cache thrashing: cache.misses spiked ~4x which increases disk reads for cold keys.
Alex: possible noisy neighbor (tenant doing large checkpoint writes). Priya, can you confirm cgroup blkio throttling or weights?
Priya: yes, blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes_recursive shows tenant cgroup hitting device write limits. blkio.weight for the tenant is default 100. Kernel shows blkio.throttle_io_service_bytes exceeded for 2 devices.
Diego: tenant 'alpha-analytics' job started an ad-hoc checkpointing run ~02:05 UTC, likely from a scheduled nightly job they kicked off. They also have an open support ticket about long-running batch ops.
Alex: immediate mitigations: (A) set per-tenant IO cap, (B) temporarily migrate tenant pods to isolated pool, (C) bump blkio.weight for other tenants, (D) enable dynamic shedding in runtime for requests that hit disk stalls. Which is least customer-impacting and fastest?
Maya: (A) or (B) fastest. IO cap via control-plane policy update takes ~90s. Migration will cause stream resets for active connections but reduces host IO quickly.
Priya: also we can throttle background checkpointing at infra level using I/O QoS shim so user job slows down. but that's slightly higher friction.
Alex: let's apply IO cap first and notify customers. Diego, can you craft a brief customer note for alpha-analytics and any affected tenants? Support-Bot, please open incident tickets.
Diego: draft note:
"We detected elevated inference latency originating from heavy disk IO by a large batch job on your instances. We are applying a temporary IO cap and may move workloads to an isolated pool. Expect partial retries for in-flight streaming requests. We'll follow up with a root cause report."
Support-Bot: Created tickets: INC-2026-5501 (alpha-analytics), INC-2026-5502 (beta-retailer), INC-2026-5503 (gamma-saas). Emails sent to ops@alpha-analytics.com
Priya: applying per-tenant IO cap via control plane: `redwoodctl policies apply --tenant alpha-analytics --blkio-write-rate 100MB/s` 90s to propagate.
Alex: apply and monitor.
(1.5m passes)
Priya: policy applied. host writeband dropped ~65%, p99 fell from 3.6s -> 1.0s, p95 improved to ~420ms. KV cache miss rate decreasing.
Maya: still seeing small tail on gpu-host-09; different tenant 'beta-retailer' also doing heavy snapshot. Looks like two noisy neighbors.
Alex: ok. next step: schedule live migration of one of the tenants. Diego, pick the less critical tenant for eviction/migration to 'isolated-gpu-2'.
Diego: initiating live migration for beta-retailer: `redwoodctl migrate --tenant beta-retailer --from shared-gpu-2 --to isolated-gpu-2 --strategy drain` 
InfraBot: migration started. note: streaming connections will be drained with a 30s graceful timeout.
Alex: monitor errors and latency.
(3m passes)
Maya: migration finished. host IO on gpu-host-09 back to baseline. overall p99 across pool now ~480ms, p95 ~350ms. streaming stalls reduced to +2% over baseline.
Alex: good. now post-incident analysis: initial root cause = concurrent tenant checkpoint/write-heavy jobs causing device-level writeback saturation -> cgroup blkio throttling -> streaming stalls and KV cache thrashing; contributory factor: lack of per-tenant IO throttles and no automated noisy-tenant eviction.
Diego: impacts: ~3 tenants saw transient streaming resets; customer-facing impact window ~14m. Ops reported increased retry rates for some SDK clients during window.
Alex: severity set Sev2. Actions to assign:
- short (1d): implement auto-apply per-tenant IO cap when device writeback > X MB/s for > 3m (Priya)
- short (2d): add alert rule 'ALERT_NOISY_IO_POOL' for sustained blkio.writeback per pool (Infra)
- medium (3d): add automated migration when a tenant exceeds io threshold for >5m (SRE)
- medium (1w): guidance & SDK retries doc for customers about streaming reconnects (Support/Product)
- long (2w): consider isolating heavy batch/ckpt workloads to dedicated pools by default (Product/Eng)
Maya: I'll collect traces, sample logs, and KV cache stats and paste into postmortem doc.
Priya: will open a small kernel-level test to validate blkio.weight adjustments don't cause starvation and propose safe defaults.
Diego: support team already requested a customer postmortem for alpha-analytics and beta-retailer.
Support-Bot: Customer acknowledgements received from alpha-analytics and beta-retailer. Tickets updated.
Alex: oncall handoff: Priya will write the postmortem and own follow-ups. I'm logging off in 45m. Priya, take it.
Priya: taking it. I'll include timeline, metrics, commands used, and proposed monitoring changes. Draft ETA 48h.
Incident-Bot: incident logged. severity=2. Incident duration ~14m. responders: Alex, Priya, Diego, Maya, Infra.
Alex: thanks team. keep eyes open for recurrence. If anything spikes, page me directly. :thumbsup:
